## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets, with accurate educational explanations and representation-specific visuals and behavior.

## Requirements
- Provide all five presets with research-grounded explanations and visible sources.
- Clearly label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV are non-cellular viruses: they have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.
- Virus presets depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, including descriptions, distinctions, and source links.

### Active
- Add preset-selection controls and selection/loading logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Verify visuals, interaction behavior, educational caveats, and visible research links.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls in `index.html` and wire selection/loading in `app.js`.
2. Implement representation-aware plate state, markup, and observatory details.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics and disable inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, and educational/source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Preset controls belong in the app markup.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add distinct virus and organism styling.

## Important Context
- Uncommitted changes exist in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; no later edits or tests were reported.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`; `tick()` currently calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Preset reference URLs include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK2263/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3074182/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/fact-sheets/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets, with accurate educational explanations and representation-specific visuals and behavior.

## Requirements
- Provide five presets with research-grounded explanations and visible sources.
- Clearly label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV are non-cellular viruses: they have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.
- Virus presets depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, including descriptions, distinctions, and source links.

### Active
- Add preset-selection controls and selection/loading logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Verify visuals, interaction behavior, educational caveats, and visible research links.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls in `index.html` and wire selection/loading in `app.js`.
2. Implement representation-aware plate state, markup, and observatory details.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics and disable inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, and educational/source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Preset controls belong in the app markup.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add distinct virus and organism styling.

## Important Context
- Uncommitted changes exist in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; no later edits or tests were reported.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`; `tick()` currently calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Preset reference URLs include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK2263/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3074182/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/fact-sheets/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets, with accurate educational explanations and representation-specific visuals and behavior.

## Requirements
- Provide five presets with research-grounded explanations and visible sources.
- Clearly label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV are non-cellular viruses: they have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.
- Virus presets depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, including descriptions, distinctions, and source links.

### Active
- Add preset-selection controls and selection/loading logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Verify visuals, interaction behavior, educational caveats, and visible research links.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls in `index.html` and wire selection/loading in `app.js`.
2. Implement representation-aware plate state, markup, and observatory details.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics and disable inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, and educational/source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Preset controls belong in the app markup.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add distinct virus and organism styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; no later edits or tests were reported.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`; `tick()` currently calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Provide accurate educational explanations, sources, and visuals that distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses.

## Requirements
- Include five presets with research-grounded explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative; distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, including descriptions, distinctions, and source links.

### Active
- Add preset-selection controls and selection/loading logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Add distinct virus and organism styling, then verify visuals, interaction behavior, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls in `index.html` and wire selection/loading in `app.js`.
2. Implement representation-aware plate state, markup, and observatory details.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics and disable inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, and educational/source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Preset controls belong in the app markup.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add distinct virus and organism styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; no later edits or tests were reported.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`; `tick()` currently calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Provide research-grounded explanations, visible sources, and visuals distinguishing cells from non-cellular viruses.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate educational explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative; distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, with descriptions, distinctions, and source links.

### Active
- Add preset-selection controls and selection/loading logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Add distinct virus and organism styling, then verify visuals, interaction behavior, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls in `index.html` and wire selection/loading in `app.js`.
2. Implement representation-aware plate state, markup, and observatory details.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics and disable inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, and educational/source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Preset controls belong in the app markup.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add distinct virus and organism styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; no later edits or tests were reported.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`; `tick()` currently calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Preset reference URLs include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3074182/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Provide research-grounded explanations, visible sources, and visuals distinguishing cells from non-cellular viruses.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate educational explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative; distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, including descriptions, distinctions, and source links.

### Active
- Add preset-selection controls and selection/loading logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Add distinct virus and organism styling, then verify visuals, interaction behavior, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls in `index.html` and wire selection/loading in `app.js`.
2. Implement representation-aware plate state, markup, and observatory details.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics and disable inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, and educational/source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Preset controls belong in the app markup.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add distinct virus and organism styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Existing uncommitted asset change; inspect before modifying.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; no later edits or tests were reported.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`; `tick()` currently calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Preset reference URLs include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3074182/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Provide research-grounded explanations, visible sources, and visuals distinguishing cells from non-cellular viruses.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate educational explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative; distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets depict nucleated erythrocytes; rat depicts a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, with descriptions, distinctions, and source links.

### Active
- Add preset-selection controls and selection/loading logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Add distinct virus and organism styling, then verify visuals, interaction behavior, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls in `index.html` and wire selection/loading in `app.js`.
2. Implement representation-aware plate state, markup, and observatory details.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics and disable inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, and educational/source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Preset controls belong in the app markup.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add distinct virus and organism styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Existing uncommitted asset change; inspect before modifying.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; no later edits or tests were reported.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`; `tick()` currently calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Preset reference URLs include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3074182/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Provide research-grounded explanations, visible sources, and visuals distinguishing cells from non-cellular viruses.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate educational explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative; distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets depict nucleated erythrocytes; rat depicts a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, with descriptions, distinctions, and source links.

### Active
- Add preset-selection controls and selection/loading logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Add distinct virus and organism styling, then verify visuals, interaction behavior, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls in `index.html` and wire selection/loading in `app.js`.
2. Implement representation-aware plate state, markup, and observatory details.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics and disable inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, and educational/source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Preset controls belong in the app markup.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add distinct virus and organism styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Existing uncommitted asset change; inspect before modifying.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; no later edits or tests were reported.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`; `tick()` currently calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Preset reference URLs include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3074182/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Provide research-grounded explanations, visible sources, and visuals that distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate educational explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative; distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets depict nucleated erythrocytes; rat depicts a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, with descriptions, distinctions, and source links.

### Active
- Add preset-selection controls and selection/loading logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Add distinct virus and organism styling, then verify visuals, interaction behavior, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls in `index.html` and wire selection/loading in `app.js`.
2. Implement representation-aware plate state, markup, and observatory details.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics and disable inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, and educational/source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Preset controls belong in the app markup.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add distinct virus and organism styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Existing uncommitted asset change; inspect before modifying.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; no later edits or tests were reported.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`; `tick()` currently calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Preset reference URLs include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3074182/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Provide research-grounded explanations, visible sources, and visuals that distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate educational explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative; distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets depict nucleated erythrocytes; rat depicts a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, with descriptions, distinctions, and source links.

### Active
- Add preset-selection controls and selection/loading logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Add distinct virus and organism styling, then verify visuals, interaction behavior, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls in `index.html` and wire selection/loading in `app.js`.
2. Implement representation-aware plate state, markup, and observatory details.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics and disable inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, and educational/source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Preset controls belong in the app markup.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add distinct virus and organism styling.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Existing uncommitted asset change; inspect before modifying.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; no later edits or tests were reported.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`; `tick()` currently calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Preset reference URLs include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3074182/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Provide research-grounded explanations, visible sources, and visuals that distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative; distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets depict nucleated erythrocytes; rat depicts a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, including descriptions, distinctions, and source links.

### Active
- Add preset-selection controls and selection/loading logic in `index.html` and `app.js`.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Add distinct virus and organism styling, then verify visuals, interaction behavior, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls in `index.html` and wire selection/loading in `app.js`.
2. Implement representation-aware plate state, markup, and observatory details.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics and disable inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, and educational/source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Preset controls belong in the app markup.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add distinct virus and organism styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg`; the image asset is an existing modified file and should be inspected before changing.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`; `tick()` currently calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Preset reference URLs include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3074182/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Provide research-grounded explanations and visuals that distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative; distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets depict nucleated erythrocytes; rat depicts a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, with descriptions, distinctions, and source links.
- Added initial markup and styling changes in `index.html` and `style.css`.

### Active
- Verify the existing diffs and complete preset selection/loading behavior.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Verify visuals, interactions, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect current diffs in `index.html`, `app.js`, and `style.css`; check `genesis-latest.jpeg` before changing it.
2. Wire preset controls and loading, then update plate rendering and observatory details for cell/virion representations.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics and disable inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, and educational/source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: App markup and preset controls.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Existing modified image asset; inspect before changing.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`, and `genesis-latest.jpeg`.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`; `tick()` currently calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Preset reference URLs include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3074182/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Provide research-grounded explanations and visuals that distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative; distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets depict nucleated erythrocytes; rat depicts a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, including descriptions, distinctions, and source links.
- Made initial markup and styling changes in `index.html` and `style.css`.
- Inspected `genesis-latest.jpeg`; its visual contents were not described in the available history.

### Active
- Inspect existing diffs and understand the modified image before changing it.
- Wire preset selection/loading and make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Verify visuals, interactions, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect current diffs in `index.html`, `app.js`, and `style.css`; review `genesis-latest.jpeg` before modifying it.
2. Wire preset controls and loading, then update plate rendering and observatory details for cell/virion representations.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics and disable inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, and educational/source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: App markup and preset controls.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Existing modified image asset; inspect before changing.

## Important Context
- Repository has uncommitted changes in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`; `tick()` currently calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Preset reference URLs include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3074182/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Provide research-grounded explanations and visuals that distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative; distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets depict nucleated erythrocytes; rat depicts a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, including descriptions, distinctions, and source URLs.
- Made initial markup and styling changes in `index.html` and `style.css`.

### Active
- Wire preset selection/loading and persist the active preset in plate state.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Verify visuals, interactions, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset selection/loading and persist the active preset in plate state.
2. Update plate rendering and observatory details for cell and virion representations.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics and disable or adapt inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, caveats, and source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: App markup; initial changes exist, but preset controls are not wired.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; initial changes exist.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Modified image asset; inspect before changing.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `makePlateState()` returns cell-oriented state, and `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`.
- Preset references include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2020.01914/full, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK2263/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3056336/.
- `cellView()` currently builds a cell-only observatory with organelles and cell-cycle information.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Provide research-grounded explanations and visuals that distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative; distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets depict nucleated erythrocytes; rat depicts a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, including descriptions, distinctions, and source URLs.
- Made initial markup and styling changes in `index.html` and `style.css`.
- Began inspecting app structure and identified cell-centric functions and mechanics.

### Active
- Wire preset selection/loading and persist the active preset in plate state.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Verify visuals, interactions, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset selection/loading and persist the active preset in plate state.
2. Update plate rendering and observatory details for cell and virion representations.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics and disable or adapt inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, caveats, and source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: App markup; initial changes exist, but preset controls are not wired.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; initial changes exist.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Modified image asset; inspect before changing.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `makePlateState()` returns cell-oriented state, and `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`.
- `cellView()` currently builds a cell-only observatory with organelles and cell-cycle information.
- Preset references include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2020.01914/full, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK2263/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3056336/.

- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Clearly distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, with descriptions, distinctions, and source URLs.
- Began markup and styling changes in `index.html` and `style.css`.

### Active
- Wire preset selection/loading and persist the active preset in plate state.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Verify visuals, interactions, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset selection/loading and persist the active preset.
2. Update plate rendering and observatory details for cell and virion representations.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics; disable or adapt inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, caveats, and source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: App markup; preset controls are not yet wired.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Modified image asset; inspect before changing.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `makePlateState()` returns cell-oriented state, and `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`.
- Preset references include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2020.01914/full, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK2263/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3056336/.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Clearly distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, including descriptions, distinctions, and source URLs.

### Active
- Wire preset selection/loading and persist the active preset in plate state.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Verify visuals, interactions, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset selection/loading and persist the active preset.
2. Update plate rendering and observatory details for cell and virion representations.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics; disable or adapt inappropriate cell-only actions.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Clearly distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, including descriptions, distinctions, and source URLs.

### Active
- Wire preset selection/loading and persist the active preset in plate state.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Verify visuals, interactions, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset selection/loading and persist the active preset.
2. Update plate rendering and observatory details for cell and virion representations.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics; disable or adapt inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, caveats, and source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: App markup; preset controls are not yet wired.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Modified image asset; inspect before changing.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `makePlateState()` returns cell-oriented state, and `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`.
- Preset references include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2020.01914/full, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK2263/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3056336/.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Clearly distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, including descriptions, distinctions, and source URLs.

### Active
- Wire preset selection/loading and persist the active preset in plate state.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Verify visuals, interactions, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset selection/loading and persist the active preset.
2. Update plate rendering and observatory details for cell and virion representations.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics; disable or adapt inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, caveats, and source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: App markup; preset controls are not yet wired.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Modified image asset; inspect before changing.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `makePlateState()` returns cell-oriented state, and `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`.
- Preset references include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2020.01914/full, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK2263/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3056336/.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Clearly distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, including descriptions, distinctions, and source URLs.

### Active
- Wire preset selection/loading and persist the active preset in plate state.
- Make plate state, `plateCellMarkup()`, and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Verify visuals, interactions, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset selection/loading and persist the active preset.
2. Update plate rendering and observatory details for cell and virion representations.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics; disable or adapt inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, caveats, and source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: App markup; preset controls are not yet wired.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Modified image asset; inspect before changing.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `makePlateState()` returns cell-oriented state, and `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Relevant functions include `makePlateState()`, `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Clearly distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, with descriptions, distinctions, and source URLs.

### Active
- Wire preset selection/loading and persist the active preset in plate state.
- Make plate rendering and observatory details representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Verify visuals, interactions, educational caveats, and visible sources.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset selection/loading and persist the active preset.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for cell and virion representations.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics; disable or adapt inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, caveats, and source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: App markup; preset controls are not yet wired.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles.
- `genesis-latest.jpeg`: Modified image asset; inspect before changing.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `makePlateState()` returns cell-oriented state, and `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Related functions include `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`.
- Preset references include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2020.01914/full, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK2263/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3056336/.

- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Clearly distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, with descriptions, distinctions, and source URLs.

### Active
- Wire preset selection/loading and persist the active preset in plate state.
- Make plate rendering and observatory details representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Verify visuals, interactions, educational caveats, and source visibility.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset selection/loading and persist the active preset.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for cell and virion representations.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics; disable or adapt inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, caveats, and source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: App markup; preset controls are not yet wired.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; inspect `genesis-latest.jpeg` before changing it.
- `makePlateState()` returns cell-oriented state, and `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Related functions include `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`.
- Preset references include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2020.01914/full, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK2263/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3056336/.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Clearly distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, with descriptions, distinctions, and source URLs.

### Active
- Wire preset selection/loading and persist the active preset in plate state.
- Make plate rendering and observatory details representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Verify visuals, interactions, educational caveats, and source visibility.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset selection/loading and persist the active preset.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for cell and virion representations.
3. Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics; disable or adapt inappropriate cell-only actions.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, caveats, and source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: App markup; preset controls are not yet wired.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; inspect `genesis-latest.jpeg` before changing it.
- `makePlateState()` returns cell-oriented state, and `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Related functions include `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`.
- Preset references include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2020.01914/full, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK2263/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3056336/.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Clearly distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS` in `app.js` for rat hepatocyte, chicken erythrocyte, tuna erythrocyte, influenza A virion, and HIV-1 virion, including descriptions and source URLs.
- Added `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`; preset selection is not yet wired to UI.

### Active
- Wire preset selection/loading and persist the active preset in plate state.
- Make plate rendering and observatory details representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics; disable or adapt inappropriate cell-only actions.
- Verify visuals, interactions, educational caveats, and source visibility.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls to the observatory and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for cell and virion representations.
3. Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, caveats, and source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data and helpers, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: App markup; preset controls are not yet wired.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; inspect `genesis-latest.jpeg` before changing it.
- `makePlateState()` is cell-oriented; `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Related functions include `addCellsToPlate()`, `plateGenome()`, `plateCellMarkup()`, `cellView()`, `advancePlateCells()`, and `dividePlateCell()`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Clearly distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`; preset data includes explanations and source URLs.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` for cells created by `makePlateState()`; virus presets create free-virion plate entries.

### Active
- Wire preset selection/loading and display the active preset’s description and sources.
- Make plate rendering and observatory details representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Prevent virus presets from using cell-cycle/division mechanics; disable or adapt inappropriate cell-only actions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls to the observatory and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for cell and virion representations, including preset explanations and sources.
3. Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, caveats, and source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data/helpers, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: App markup; preset controls are not yet wired.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; inspect `genesis-latest.jpeg` before changing it.
- `tick()` currently calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally; `advancePlateCells()` updates cell metrics and can divide cells.
- `cellView()` and `plateCellMarkup()` currently assume cellular measurements and organelles; actions include `plate-live`, `plate-archive`, `cell-cycle`, `stain`, `remove-cell`, `inspect-genome`, and `add-element-plate`.
- Preset references include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2020.01914/full, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK2263/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3056336/.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Clearly distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`; preset data includes explanations and source URLs.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` for cells created by `makePlateState()`; virus presets create free-virion plate entries.

### Active
- Wire preset selection/loading and display the active preset’s description and sources.
- Make `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Test presets, visuals, behavior, caveats, and source visibility.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls to the observatory and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for cell and virion representations, including preset explanations and sources.
3. Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
4. Test presets, visuals, behavior, caveats, and source visibility.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data/helpers, plate state, rendering, observatory view, and action handling.
- `index.html`: App markup; preset controls are not yet wired.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; inspect `genesis-latest.jpeg` before changing it.
- `tick()` currently calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally; `advancePlateCells()` updates cell metrics and can divide cells.
- `cellView()` and `plateCellMarkup()` currently assume cellular measurements and organelles; actions include `plate-live`, `plate-archive`, `cell-cycle`, `stain`, `remove-cell`, `inspect-genome`, and `add-element-plate`.
- Preset references include https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK541055/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34378417/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10179511/, https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2020.01914/full, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483285/, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK2263/, https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle, and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3056336/.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Clearly distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`; preset data includes explanations and source URLs.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`; virus presets create free-virion plate entries.
- Inspected current plate rendering, observatory markup, actions, and simulation tick behavior to identify integration points.

### Active
- Wire preset selection/loading and display the active preset’s description and sources.
- Make `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Test presets, visuals, behavior, caveats, and source visibility.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls to the observatory and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` to render cells and virions appropriately, including preset explanations and sources.
3. Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions when a virus preset is active.
4. Test preset loading, rendering, behavior, caveats, and visible citations.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data/helpers, plate state, rendering, tick advancement, and action handling.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add virion/preset styling as needed.
- `index.html`: App shell; observatory content is rendered by `app.js`.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; the image has not been inspected for changes.
- `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally; `advancePlateCells()` updates cell metrics and can divide cells.
- `cellView()` and `plateCellMarkup()` currently assume cellular measurements and organelles; cell-only actions include `plate-live`, `plate-archive`, `cell-cycle`, `stain`, `remove-cell`, `inspect-genome`, and `add-element-plate`.
- Current HIV source URL in `PLATE_PRESETS` is `https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/fact-sheets/hiv-life-cycle`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Clearly distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`; preset data includes explanations and source URLs.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`; virus presets create free-virion plate entries.
- Inspected plate rendering, observatory markup, actions, and simulation tick behavior to identify integration points.

### Active
- Wire preset selection/loading and display the active preset’s description and sources.
- Make `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` representation-aware for cells versus virions.
- Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions when a virus preset is active.
- Test preset loading, rendering, behavior, caveats, and source visibility.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls to the observatory and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` to render cells and virions appropriately, including preset explanations and sources.
3. Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions when a virus preset is active.
4. Test preset loading, visuals, behavior, caveats, and visible citations.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data/helpers, plate state, rendering, tick advancement, and action handling.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add virion/preset styling as needed.
- `index.html`: App shell; observatory content is rendered by `app.js`.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; the image has not been inspected for changes.
- `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally; `advancePlateCells()` updates cell metrics and can divide cells.
- `cellView()` and `plateCellMarkup()` currently assume cellular measurements and organelles; cell-only actions include `plate-live`, `plate-archive`, `cell-cycle`, `stain`, `remove-cell`, `inspect-genome`, and `add-element-plate`.
- Current HIV source URL in `PLATE_PRESETS` is `https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/fact-sheets/hiv-life-cycle`.
