messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`, including explanations and source URLs.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`; virus presets create free-virion plate entries.
- Inspected plate rendering, simulation advancement, actions, and observatory markup to identify integration points.

### Active
- Add preset selection/loading controls and display the selected preset’s description and citations.
- Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` to render cells versus virions appropriately.
- Prevent virus entries from cellular advancement/division and guard cell-only actions when a virus preset is active.
- Test preset loading, rendering, behavior, caveats, and visible citations.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add observatory preset controls and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virion rendering and preset descriptions/source links.
3. Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
4. Test all five presets, including persistence, visible citations, and non-cellular behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data/helpers, plate rendering, tick advancement, and action handling.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add virion/preset styling.
- `index.html`: App shell; observatory content is rendered by `app.js`.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; the image change has not been inspected.
- `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally; that function updates cellular metrics and can divide cells.
- Cell-only actions include `plate-live`, `plate-archive`, `cell-cycle`, `stain`, `remove-cell`, `inspect-genome`, and `add-element-plate`.
- HIV source URL: `https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/fact-sheets/hiv-life-cycle`.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`, including explanations and source URLs.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`; virus presets create free-virion plate entries.
- Inspected plate rendering, simulation advancement, actions, and observatory markup for integration points.

### Active
- Add preset selection/loading controls and display the selected preset’s description and citations.
- Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` to render cells versus virions appropriately.
- Prevent virus entries from cellular advancement/division and guard cell-only actions when a virus preset is active.
- Test preset loading, rendering, behavior, caveats, and visible citations.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add observatory preset controls and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virion rendering and preset descriptions/source links.
3. Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
4. Test all five presets, including persistence, visible citations, and non-cellular behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data/helpers, plate rendering, tick advancement, and action handling.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add virion/preset styling.
- `index.html`: App shell; observatory content is rendered by `app.js`.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; the image change has not been inspected.
- `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally; that function updates cellular metrics and can divide cells.
- Cell-only actions include `plate-live`, `plate-archive`, `cell-cycle`, `stain`, `remove-cell`, `inspect-genome`, and `add-element-plate`.
- HIV source URL: `https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/fact-sheets/hiv-life-cycle`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`, including explanations and source URLs.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`; virus presets create free-virion plate entries.
- Inspected plate rendering, simulation advancement, actions, and observatory markup for integration points.

### Active
- Add preset selection/loading controls and display the selected preset’s description and citations.
- Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` to render cells versus virions appropriately.
- Prevent virus entries from cellular advancement/division and guard cell-only actions when a virus preset is active.
- Test preset loading, rendering, behavior, caveats, and visible citations.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add observatory preset controls and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virion rendering and preset descriptions/source links.
3. Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
4. Test all five presets, including persistence, visible citations, and non-cellular behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data/helpers, plate rendering, tick advancement, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Observatory markup and potential location for preset controls.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add virion/preset styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; the image change has not been inspected.
- `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally; that function updates cellular metrics and can divide cells.
- Cell-only actions include `plate-live`, `plate-archive`, `cell-cycle`, `stain`, `remove-cell`, `inspect-genome`, and `add-element-plate`.
- HIV source URL: `https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/fact-sheets/hiv-life-cycle`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Clearly distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`, including explanations and source URLs.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added two lines to `index.html` and modified plate styles in `style.css`.
- Inspected plate rendering, simulation advancement, actions, and observatory markup for integration points.

### Active
- Add preset selection/loading controls and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
- Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virion rendering and preset descriptions/source links.
- Guard virus entries from cellular advancement/division and guard cell-only actions when a virus preset is active.
- Test all five presets, including persistence, visible citations, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add observatory preset controls and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virion rendering and preset descriptions/source links.
3. Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
4. Test preset loading, rendering, behavior, caveats, and visible citations.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data/helpers, plate rendering, tick advancement, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Observatory markup and potential location for preset controls.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add virion/preset styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; the image change has not been inspected.
- `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally; that function updates cellular metrics and can divide cells.
- Cell-only actions include `plate-live`, `plate-archive`, `cell-cycle`, `stain`, `remove-cell`, `inspect-genome`, and `add-element-plate`.
- HIV source URL: `https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/fact-sheets/hiv-life-cycle`.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Clearly distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`, including explanations and source URLs.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added two lines to `index.html` and modified plate styles in `style.css`.
- Inspected plate rendering, simulation advancement, actions, and observatory markup integration points.

### Active
- Add observatory preset selection/loading controls and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
- Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virion rendering and preset descriptions/source links.
- Guard virus entries from cellular advancement/division and guard cell-only actions when a virus preset is active.
- Test all five presets, including persistence, visible citations, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add observatory preset controls and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virion rendering and preset descriptions/source links.
3. Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
4. Test preset loading, rendering, behavior, caveats, and visible citations.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data/helpers, plate rendering, tick advancement, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Observatory markup and potential location for preset controls.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add virion/preset styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; the image change has not been inspected.
- `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally; that function updates cellular metrics and can divide cells.

- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Clearly distinguish cells from non-cellular viruses while preserving existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`, including explanations and source URLs.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added two lines to `index.html` and modified plate styles in `style.css`.
- Inspected plate rendering, simulation advancement, actions, and observatory markup integration points.

### Active
- Add observatory preset selection/loading controls and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
- Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virion rendering and preset descriptions/source links.
- Guard virus entries from cellular advancement/division and guard cell-only actions when a virus preset is active.
- Test all five presets, including persistence, visible citations, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add observatory preset controls and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virion rendering and preset descriptions/source links.
3. Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
4. Test preset loading, rendering, behavior, caveats, and visible citations.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data/helpers, plate rendering, tick advancement, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Observatory markup and potential location for preset controls.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add virion/preset styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; the image change has not been inspected.
- `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally; that function updates cellular metrics and can divide cells.
- Cell-only actions include `plate-live`, `plate-archive`, `cell-cycle`, `stain`, `remove-cell`, `inspect-genome`, and `add-element-plate`.
- HIV source URL: `https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/fact-sheets/hiv-life-cycle`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets.
- Distinguish cellular and viral entities while preserving the existing educational features.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Label simplified mechanics as illustrative and distinguish viruses from cells.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`, including explanations and source URLs.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Made initial markup/style changes in `index.html` and `style.css`.
- Inspected plate rendering, simulation advancement, actions, and observatory markup integration points.

### Active
- Add observatory preset selection/loading controls and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
- Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virion rendering, preset descriptions, and source links.
- Guard virus entries from cellular advancement/division and guard cell-only actions when a virus preset is active.
- Test all five presets for loading, rendering, persistence, citations, caveats, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add observatory preset controls and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virion rendering and preset descriptions/source links.
3. Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
4. Test preset loading, rendering, behavior, caveats, persistence, and visible citations.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data/helpers, plate rendering, tick advancement, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Observatory markup and potential location for preset controls.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add virion/preset styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; the image change has not been inspected.
- `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally; it updates cellular metrics and can divide cells.
- Cell-only actions include `plate-live`, `plate-archive`, `cell-cycle`, `stain`, `remove-cell`, `inspect-genome`, and `add-element-plate`.
- HIV source URL: `https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/fact-sheets/hiv-life-cycle`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Clearly distinguish cells from viruses and label simplified mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions—not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`, including explanations and source URLs.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Made initial markup/style changes in `index.html` and `style.css`.

### Active
- Add observatory preset selection/loading controls and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
- Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virion rendering, preset descriptions, and source links.
- Guard virus entries from cellular advancement/division and guard cell-only actions when a virus preset is active.
- Test preset loading, rendering, behavior, caveats, persistence, and visible citations.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add observatory preset controls and wire them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virions, preset descriptions, and source links.
3. Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
4. Test all five presets, including persistence, visible citations, and non-cellular behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data/helpers, plate rendering, tick advancement, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Observatory markup and location for preset controls.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add virion/preset styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; the image change has not been inspected.
- `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally; it updates cellular metrics and can divide cells.
- Cell-only actions include `plate-live`, `plate-archive`, `cell-cycle`, `stain`, `remove-cell`, `inspect-genome`, and `add-element-plate`.
- HIV source URL: `https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle`.
- `plateCellMarkup()` is at `app.js:93`; `cellView()` is at `app.js:97`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Clearly distinguish cells from viruses and label simplified mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.

## Decisions
- Influenza and HIV presets represent free virions—not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`, including explanations and source URLs.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Began initial markup and style changes in `index.html` and `style.css`.

### Active
- Add observatory preset selection/loading controls and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
- Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virion rendering, preset descriptions, and source links.
- Guard virus entries from cellular advancement/division and guard cell-only actions when a virus preset is active.
- Test preset loading, rendering, behavior, caveats, persistence, and visible citations.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add observatory preset controls and wire them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virions, preset descriptions, and source links.
3. Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
4. Test all five presets, including persistence, visible citations, and non-cellular behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data/helpers, plate rendering, tick advancement, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Observatory markup and location for preset controls.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add virion/preset styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; the image change has not been inspected.
- `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally; it updates cellular metrics and can divide cells.
- Cell-only actions include `plate-live`, `plate-archive`, `cell-cycle`, `stain`, `remove-cell`, `inspect-genome`, and `add-element-plate`.
- HIV source URL: `https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle`.
- `plateCellMarkup()` is at `app.js:93`; `cellView()` is at `app.js:97`.

- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Clearly distinguish cells from viruses and label simplified mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Represent influenza and HIV as free virions—not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Represent bird and tuna as nucleated erythrocytes, and rat as a hepatocyte rather than a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets should not show cellular metrics or organelles.
- Virus presets should not advance or divide through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`, with explanations and source URLs.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.

### Active
- Add preset selection/loading controls to the observatory and wire them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
- Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virion rendering, preset descriptions, and visible citations.
- Prevent virus entries from cellular advancement/division and guard cell-only actions.
- Test preset loading, rendering, behavior, caveats, persistence, and visible citations.

### Blocked
- None.

1. Add observatory preset controls and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Update plate rendering and details for virions versus cells, including preset descriptions and source links.
3. Guard cell advancement/division and cell-only actions for virus presets.
4. Test all five presets, persistence, citations, and non-cellular behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data/helpers, plate rendering, tick advancement, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Observatory markup and location for preset controls.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add virion/preset styling.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Clearly distinguish cells from free virions and label simplified mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Represent influenza and HIV as free virions—not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Represent bird and tuna as nucleated erythrocytes, and rat as a hepatocyte rather than a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets should not show cellular metrics or organelles.
- Virus presets should not advance or divide through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, and `loadPlatePreset()` in `app.js`.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.

### Active
- Add observatory preset selection/loading controls and wire them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
- Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virion rendering, preset descriptions, and visible citations.
- Prevent virus entries from cellular advancement/division and guard cell-only actions.
- Test preset loading, rendering, behavior, caveats, persistence, and visible citations.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls to the observatory in `index.html` and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Update `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` in `app.js` for distinct virion rendering/details, preset descriptions, and source links.
3. Guard `advancePlateCells()`, division, and cell-only actions for virus presets.
4. Test all five presets, persistence, citations, and non-cellular behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data/helpers, plate rendering, tick advancement, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Observatory markup and location for preset controls.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add virion/preset styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; the image change has not been inspected.
- `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally; it updates cellular metrics and can divide cells.
- Cell-only actions include `plate-live`, `plate-archive`, `cell-cycle`, `stain`, `remove-cell`, `inspect-genome`, and `add-element-plate`.
- HIV source URL in preset data: `https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Clearly distinguish cells from free virions and label simplified mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Influenza and HIV presets must depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression; viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets must represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat must represent a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets should show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- Virus presets must not advance or divide through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup to `index.html`.

### Active
- Add preset selection/loading controls to the observatory and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
- Update plate rendering and `cellView()` for virions, preset descriptions, citations, and cell-only versus virus-only details.
- Guard cellular simulation, division, and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Test presets, persistence, citations, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls to the observatory markup in `app.js`’s `cellView()` and wire clicks to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Branch `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` on the active preset/entity kind; render visible explanations and citations.
3. Prevent virus entries from advancing or dividing in `advancePlateCells()`/`tick()` and guard cell-only actions in `handleAction()`.
4. Test all five presets, persistence, citations, and virus behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data/helpers, plate rendering, simulation advancement, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Navigation and researcher progression markup.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add virion/preset styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; the image change has not been inspected.
- `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally; that function updates cellular metrics and can divide cells.
- Cell-only actions include `plate-live`, `plate-archive`, `cell-cycle`, `stain`, `remove-cell`, `inspect-genome`, and `add-element-plate`.
- `cellView()` currently assumes every plate entry has cellular metrics and organelles; `plateCellMarkup()` likewise renders all entries as cells.
- `loadPlatePreset()` stores and renders the selected preset and shows a toast distinguishing free virions from illustrative cellular presets.
- HIV source currently uses `https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle`; the preset data also includes a fact-sheet link.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s seeded plate with selectable rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Clearly distinguish cells from free virions and label simplified mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Influenza and HIV presets must depict free virions—not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Bird and tuna presets must represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat must represent a hepatocyte, not a mature mammalian red blood cell.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets should show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- Virus presets must not advance or divide through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup to `index.html`.

### Active
- Add preset selection/loading controls to the observatory in `app.js`’s `cellView()` and connect them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
- Update plate rendering and `cellView()` to distinguish virions, show preset explanations and citations, and display only relevant cell- or virus-specific details.
- Guard cellular simulation, division, and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Test all presets, persistence, citations, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add preset controls to the observatory markup in `cellView()` and wire them to `loadPlatePreset()`.
2. Branch `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` on the active preset/entity kind; render visible explanations and citations.
3. Prevent virus entries from advancing or dividing in `advancePlateCells()`/`tick()` and guard cell-only actions in `handleAction()`.
4. Test presets, persistence, citations, and virus behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Preset data/helpers, plate rendering, simulation advancement, and action handling.
- `index.html`: Navigation and researcher progression markup.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; add virion/preset styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`; the image change has not been inspected.
- `tick()` calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally; that function updates cellular metrics and can divide cells.
- Cell-only actions include `plate-live`, `plate-archive`, `cell-cycle`, `stain`, `remove-cell`, `inspect-genome`, and `add-element-plate`.
- `cellView()` and `plateCellMarkup()` currently assume every plate entry has cellular metrics and organelles.
- `loadPlatePreset()` stores and renders the selected preset and shows a toast distinguishing free virions from illustrative cellular presets.
- HIV source currently uses `https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/hiv-life-cycle`; preset data also includes a fact-sheet link.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s plate with rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Clearly distinguish cells from free virions and label simplified mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Bird and tuna presets must represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat must represent a hepatocyte.
- Influenza and HIV presets must depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Virus presets must not advance or divide through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- `loadPlatePreset()` distinguishes free virions from illustrative cellular presets in its toast.
- Virus plate entries are intended to be static particle schematics; no infection or division is modeled.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `PLATE_PRESETS`, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup to `index.html`.
- Reworked `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` to render virus-aware plate items, preset selection controls, preset explanations/citations, and separate virus/cell details.

### Active
- Wire preset buttons to `loadPlatePreset()` and verify preset selection and persistence.
- Add appropriate virion, bird-erythrocyte, and tuna-erythrocyte styling in `style.css`.
- Guard cellular simulation, division, and cell-only actions for virus presets.
- Ensure periodic-table element actions are disabled or safely unavailable for virions.
- Test all presets, citations, persistence, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s plate with rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Clearly distinguish cells from free virions and label simplified mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Bird and tuna presets must represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat must represent a hepatocyte.
- Influenza and HIV presets must depict free virions—not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Virus presets must not advance or divide through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- `loadPlatePreset()` distinguishes free virions from illustrative cellular presets in its toast.
- Virus plate entries are intended as static particle schematics; no infection or division is modeled.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added five preset definitions, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup in `index.html`.
- Reworked `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virus-aware content, preset controls, explanations/citations, and separate virus/cell details.
- `node --check app.js` passes.
- Confirmed virus view hides cell-only action buttons and cell metrics; it passes `!virus` to `elementResultMarkup()`.

### Active
- Wire and verify preset selection and event handling; no handler wiring for `load-plate-preset` was found in the inspected code.
- Guard `tick()` and cell-only actions for virus presets; `tick()` still calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Verify `elementResultMarkup()` exists and disables virion element actions; its implementation and event handlers remain uninspected.
- Add and verify virion, bird-erythrocyte, and tuna-erythrocyte styling; current CSS search did not show these selectors.
- Test preset selection, citations, persistence, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining event wiring and `elementResultMarkup()` in `app.js`; connect preset controls and add virus guards to simulation and cell-only actions.
2. Add missing virion and erythrocyte styling in `style.css`.
3. Run syntax and behavior checks across all five presets.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Presets, plate rendering, simulation, actions, and periodic-table markup.
- `index.html`: DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; needs preset and virion styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `cellView()` includes free-virion details and citations, but hides cell-only controls for virus presets.
- `tick()` unconditionally advances plate cells, so static-virus behavior is not yet guaranteed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s plate with rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Distinguish cells from free virions and label simplified mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Bird and tuna presets must represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat must represent a hepatocyte.
- Influenza and HIV presets must depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Virus presets must not advance or divide through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- `loadPlatePreset()` distinguishes free virions from illustrative cellular presets in its toast.
- Virus plate entries are static particle schematics; no infection or division is modeled.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added five preset definitions, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup in `index.html`.
- Reworked `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virus-aware content, preset controls, explanations/citations, and separate virus/cell details.
- Virus view hides cell-only actions and cell metrics, and calls `elementResultMarkup(!virus)`.
- Latest inspection confirmed `plateCellMarkup()` applies virus, bird/tuna erythrocyte, and other visual classes; styles and behavior still need verification.

### Active
- Inspect event handlers and `elementResultMarkup()`; preset button wiring and element actions remain unverified.
- Guard simulation and cell-only actions for virus presets: `tick()` still calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Verify virion, bird-erythrocyte, and tuna-erythrocyte styling in `style.css`.
- Test preset selection, citations, persistence, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect event handling and `elementResultMarkup()` in `app.js`; wire preset controls and guard simulation and cell-only actions for viruses.
2. Verify or add missing virion and erythrocyte styling in `style.css`.
3. Run syntax and behavior checks across all five presets.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Presets, rendering, simulation, actions, periodic-table markup, and event handling.
- `index.html`: DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; needs preset and virion styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `tick()` still advances plate cells unconditionally; static-virus behavior is not guaranteed yet.
- `cellView()` handles virus display, but its event wiring and element-action behavior have not been verified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s plate with rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Distinguish cells from free virions and label simplified mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Bird and tuna presets must represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat must represent a hepatocyte.
- Influenza and HIV presets must depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Virus presets must not advance or divide through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- `loadPlatePreset()` distinguishes free virions from illustrative cellular presets in its toast.
- Virus plate entries are static particle schematics; no infection or division is modeled.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added five preset definitions, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup in `index.html`.
- Reworked `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` for virus-aware content, preset controls, explanations/citations, and separate virus/cell details.
- `node --check app.js` completed without syntax errors.

### Active
- Verify event handlers, preset control wiring, `elementResultMarkup()` behavior, and guard cell-only actions for virus presets.
- `tick()` still calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally; static-virus behavior is not guaranteed.
- Verify or add virion and bird/tuna erythrocyte styling in `style.css`.
- Test preset selection, citations, persistence, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect event handling and `elementResultMarkup()` in `app.js`; wire preset controls and guard simulation and cell-only actions for viruses.
2. Verify or add missing virion and erythrocyte styling in `style.css`.
3. Run syntax and behavior checks across all five presets.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Presets, rendering, simulation, actions, periodic-table markup, and event handling.
- `index.html`: DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; needs preset and virion styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- Latest inspection found no event handler or `elementResultMarkup()` verification yet; `plateCellMarkup()` applies virus, bird/tuna erythrocyte, and other visual classes.

- Influenza and HIV presets must depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets show no cellular metrics or organelles.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s plate with rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Distinguish cells from free virions and label simplified cellular mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte.
- Influenza and HIV depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Virus presets must not advance or divide through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- `loadPlatePreset()` distinguishes free virions from illustrative cellular presets in its toast.
- Virus plate entries are static particle schematics; no infection or division is modeled.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added five preset definitions, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup in `index.html`.
- Updated `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` with virus-aware content, preset controls, explanations/citations, and separate virus/cell details.
- `node --check app.js` completed without syntax errors.

### Active
- Restore or implement rendering, navigation, and event-handler wiring in `app.js`; no `addEventListener`, `onclick`, or `function render` was found, and the file ends at `genomeView()`.
- Guard simulation and all cell-only actions for virus presets; `tick()` still calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Verify or add virion, erythrocyte, and preset-control styles in `style.css`.
- Test preset selection, citations, persistence, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and restore/implement rendering and event handling, including preset selection and virus simulation/action guards.
2. Verify or add the required virion, erythrocyte, and preset styles.
3. Run syntax and behavior checks across all five presets.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Presets, rendering, simulation, actions, periodic-table markup, and missing app wiring.
- `index.html`: Navigation, DNA Codex, researcher progression, and app mount point.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; preset and virion styling remains unverified.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `elementResultMarkup()` exists, but its behavior has not been verified.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s plate with rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Distinguish cells from free virions and label simplified cellular mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte.
- Influenza and HIV depict free virions—not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Virus presets must not advance or divide through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- `loadPlatePreset()` distinguishes free virions from illustrative cellular presets in its toast.
- Virus plate entries are static particle schematics; no infection or division is modeled.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added five preset definitions, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`.
- Added `entityKind:'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup in `index.html`.
- Updated `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` with virus-aware content, preset controls, explanations/citations, and separate virus/cell details.
- `node --check app.js` completed without syntax errors.

### Active
- Restore or implement rendering, navigation, and event-handler wiring in `app.js`; no `addEventListener`, `onclick`, or `function render` was found, and the file ends at `genomeView()`.
- Guard simulation and all cell-only actions for virus presets; `tick()` still calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Verify or add virion, erythrocyte, and preset-control styles in `style.css`.
- Test preset selection, citations, persistence, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and restore/implement rendering and event handling, including preset selection and virus simulation/action guards.
2. Verify or add the required virion, erythrocyte, and preset styles.
3. Run syntax and behavior checks across all five presets.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Presets, rendering, simulation, actions, periodic-table markup, and missing app wiring.
- `index.html`: Navigation, DNA Codex, researcher progression, and app mount point.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; preset and virion styling remains unverified.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `elementResultMarkup()` exists, but its behavior has not been verified.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s plate with rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Distinguish cells from free virions and label simplified cellular mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte.
- Influenza and HIV depict free virions—not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Virus presets must not advance or divide through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- `loadPlatePreset()` distinguishes free virions from illustrative cellular presets in its toast.
- Virus plate entries are static particle schematics; no infection or division is modeled.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added five preset definitions, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`.
- Added `entityKind: 'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.

- Updated `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` with virus-aware content, preset controls, explanations/citations, and separate virus/cell details.
- `node --check app.js` completed without syntax errors.

### Active
- Restore or implement rendering, navigation, and event-handler wiring in `app.js`; current file ends at `genomeView()` and has no `render()`, event listeners, or app initialization.
- Guard simulation and all cell-only actions for virus presets; `tick()` still calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Verify or add virion, erythrocyte, and preset-control styles in `style.css`.
- Test preset selection, citations, persistence, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Restore/implement the missing app views and wiring in `app.js`, integrating the existing presets.
2. Prevent virus presets from advancing/dividing or invoking cell-only actions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Presets, rendering, simulation, actions, and missing app wiring.
- `index.html`: Navigation, DNA Codex, researcher progression, and app mount point.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; preset and virion styling remains unverified.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `git show HEAD:app.js` includes older event-handler and rendering code, but not the current preset additions; use it as a reference rather than overwriting current work.
- `elementResultMarkup()` was not verified.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS’s plate with rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Clearly distinguish cells from free virions and label simplified cellular mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte.
- Influenza and HIV depict free virions—not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Virus presets must not advance or divide through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- `loadPlatePreset()` distinguishes free virions from illustrative cellular presets in its toast.
- Virus plate entries are static particle schematics; no infection or division is modeled.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added five preset definitions, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`.
- Added `entityKind: 'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup in `index.html`.
- Updated `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` with virus-aware content, preset controls, explanations/citations, and separate virus/cell details.
- `node --check app.js` completed without syntax errors.

### Active
- Restore or implement rendering, navigation, and event-handler wiring in `app.js`; current file ends at `genomeView()` and has no `render()`, event listeners, or app initialization.
- Guard simulation and all cell-only actions for virus presets; `tick()` still calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Verify or add virion, erythrocyte, and preset-control styles in `style.css`.
- Test preset selection, citations, persistence, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore or implement missing app views and wiring in `app.js`, integrating the existing presets.
2. Prevent virus presets from advancing/dividing or invoking cell-only actions.
3. Verify styles and test all presets, citations, navigation, and persistence.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Presets, rendering, simulation, actions, and missing app wiring.
- `index.html`: Navigation, DNA Codex, researcher progression, and app mount point.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; preset and virion styling remains unverified.
- `/tmp/opencode/old-app.js`: Saved `HEAD:app.js` for reference to previous rendering, handlers, and initialization.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `git show HEAD:app.js` contains older event-handler and rendering code, but not the current preset additions; `/tmp/opencode/old-app.js` is a saved copy for reference, not a replacement.
- `elementResultMarkup()` was not verified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Clearly distinguish cells from free virions and label simplified cellular mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte.
- Influenza and HIV depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Virus presets must not advance or divide through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- `loadPlatePreset()` distinguishes free virions from illustrative cellular presets in its toast.
- Virus plate entries are static particle schematics; no infection or division is modeled.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added five preset definitions, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`.
- Added `entityKind: 'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup in `index.html`.
- Updated `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` with virus-aware content, preset controls, explanations, citations, and separate virus/cell details.
- `node --check app.js` completed without syntax errors.

### Active
- Restore or implement rendering, navigation, and event-handler wiring in `app.js`; current file ends at `genomeView()` and has no `render()`, event listeners, or app initialization.
- Guard simulation and all cell-only actions for virus presets; `tick()` still calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Verify or add virion, erythrocyte, and preset-control styles in `style.css`.
- Test preset selection, citations, persistence, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore or implement missing app views and wiring in `app.js`, integrating the existing presets.
2. Prevent virus presets from advancing/dividing or invoking cell-only actions.
3. Verify styles and test all presets, citations, navigation, and persistence.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Presets, rendering, simulation, actions, and missing app wiring.
- `index.html`: Navigation, DNA Codex, researcher progression, and app mount point.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; preset and virion styling remains unverified.
- `/tmp/opencode/old-app.js`: Saved earlier `HEAD:app.js` for reference to rendering, handlers, and initialization.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `git show HEAD:app.js` contains older event-handler and rendering code, but not the current preset additions; `/tmp/opencode/old-app.js` is a saved reference, not a replacement.
- `elementResultMarkup()` was not verified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Distinguish cells from free virions and label simplified cellular mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte.
- Influenza and HIV depict free virions—not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Virus presets must not advance through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- `loadPlatePreset()` distinguishes free virions from illustrative cellular presets in its toast.
- Virus plate entries are static particle schematics; no infection or division is modeled.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added five preset definitions, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`.
- Added `entityKind: 'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup in `index.html`.
- Updated `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` with virus-aware content, preset controls, explanations, citations, and separate virus/cell details.
- `node --check app.js` completed without syntax errors.

### Active
- Restore or implement rendering, navigation, event-handler wiring, and app initialization in `app.js`; the current file ends at `genomeView()`.
- Guard simulation and all cell-only actions for virus presets; `tick()` still calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Verify or add virion, erythrocyte, and preset-control styles in `style.css`.
- Test preset selection, citations, persistence, navigation, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore or implement missing app views and wiring in `app.js`, integrating the existing presets.
2. Prevent virus presets from advancing/dividing or invoking cell-only actions.
3. Verify styles and test all presets, citations, navigation, and persistence.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Presets, rendering, simulation, actions, and missing app wiring.
- `index.html`: Navigation, DNA Codex, researcher progression, and app mount point.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; preset and virion styling remains unverified.
- `/tmp/opencode/old-app.js`: Saved earlier `HEAD:app.js` reference for rendering, handlers, and initialization.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `git show HEAD:app.js` contains older event-handler and rendering code, but not the current preset additions; `/tmp/opencode/old-app.js` is a saved reference, not a replacement.
- `elementResultMarkup()` was not verified.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Distinguish cells from free virions and label simplified cellular mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte.
- Influenza and HIV depict free virions—not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Virus presets must not advance through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- `loadPlatePreset()` distinguishes free virions from illustrative cellular presets in its toast.
- Virus plate entries are static particle schematics; no infection or division is modeled.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added five preset definitions, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`.
- Added `entityKind: 'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup in `index.html`.
- Updated `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` with virus-aware content, preset controls, explanations, citations, and separate virus/cell details.
- `node --check app.js` completed without syntax errors.

### Active
- Restore or implement missing rendering, navigation, event-handler wiring, and app initialization in `app.js`; current file ends at `genomeView()`.
- Guard simulation and all cell-only actions for virus presets; `tick()` still calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Verify or add virion, erythrocyte, and preset-control styles in `style.css`.
- Test preset selection, citations, persistence, navigation, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore or implement missing app views and wiring in `app.js`, integrating the existing presets.
2. Prevent virus presets from advancing/dividing or invoking cell-only actions.
3. Verify styles and test all presets, citations, navigation, and persistence.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Presets, rendering, simulation, actions, and missing app wiring.
- `index.html`: Navigation, DNA Codex, researcher progression, and app mount point.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; preset and virion styling remains unverified.
- `/tmp/opencode/old-app.js`: Saved earlier `HEAD:app.js` reference for rendering, handlers, and initialization.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `git show HEAD:app.js` contains older event-handler and rendering code, but not the current preset additions; `/tmp/opencode/old-app.js` is a reference, not a replacement.
- `elementResultMarkup()` was not verified.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Clearly distinguish cells from free virions and label simplified cellular mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte.
- Influenza and HIV depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Virus presets must not advance through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- `loadPlatePreset()` distinguishes free virions from illustrative cellular presets in its toast.
- Virus plate entries are static particle schematics; no infection or division is modeled.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added five preset definitions, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`.

- `app.js`: Presets, rendering, simulation, and missing app wiring.

- Extend GENESIS with rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Distinguish cellular presets from free virions and label simplified cellular mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte.
- Influenza and HIV depict free virions, not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Virus presets must not advance through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- `loadPlatePreset()` distinguishes free virions from illustrative cellular presets in its toast.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Clearly distinguish cellular presets from free virions and label simplified cellular mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte.
- Influenza and HIV depict free virions—not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Virus presets must not advance through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- `loadPlatePreset()` distinguishes free virions from illustrative cellular presets in its toast.
- Virus plate entries are static particle schematics; no infection or division is modeled.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added five preset definitions, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`.
- Added `entityKind: 'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup in `index.html`.
- Updated `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` with virus-aware content, preset controls, explanations, citations, and separate virus/cell details.
- `node --check app.js` completed without syntax errors.

### Active
- Restore or implement missing rendering, navigation, event-handler wiring, and app initialization in `app.js`; current file ends at `genomeView()`.
- Guard simulation and all cell-only actions for virus presets; `tick()` still calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Verify or add virion, erythrocyte, and preset-control styles in `style.css`.
- Test preset selection, citations, persistence, navigation, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore or implement app views and wiring in `app.js`, integrating existing presets.
2. Prevent virus presets from advancing/dividing or invoking cell-only actions.
3. Verify styles and test all presets, citations, navigation, and persistence.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Presets, rendering, simulation, and missing app wiring.
- `index.html`: Navigation, DNA Codex, researcher progression, and app mount point.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; preset and virion styling remains unverified.
- `/tmp/opencode/old-app.js`: Saved earlier `HEAD:app.js` reference for rendering, handlers, and initialization.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `git show HEAD:app.js` contains older event-handler and rendering code, but not the current preset additions; `/tmp/opencode/old-app.js` is a reference, not a replacement.
- `elementResultMarkup()` was not verified.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Distinguish cellular presets from free virions and label simplified cellular mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte.
- Influenza and HIV depict free virions—not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Virus presets must not advance through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- `loadPlatePreset()` distinguishes free virions from illustrative cellular presets in its toast.
- Virus plate entries are static particle schematics; no infection or division is modeled.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added five preset definitions, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`.
- Added `entityKind: 'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup in `index.html`.
- Updated `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` with virus-aware content, preset controls, explanations, citations, and separate virus/cell details.
- `node --check app.js` completed without syntax errors.

### Active
- Restore or implement missing rendering, navigation, event-handler wiring, and app initialization in `app.js`; current file ends at `genomeView()`.
- Guard simulation and all cell-only actions for virus presets; `tick()` still calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Verify or add virion, erythrocyte, and preset-control styles in `style.css`.
- Test preset selection, citations, persistence, navigation, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore or implement app views and wiring in `app.js`, integrating existing presets.
2. Prevent virus presets from advancing/dividing or invoking cell-only actions.
3. Verify styles and test all presets, citations, navigation, and persistence.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Presets, rendering, simulation, and missing app wiring.
- `index.html`: Navigation, DNA Codex, researcher progression, and app mount point.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; preset and virion styling remains unverified.
- `/tmp/opencode/old-app.js`: Saved earlier `HEAD:app.js` reference for rendering, handlers, and initialization.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- The current `app.js` is only 97 lines; `git show HEAD:app.js` and `/tmp/opencode/old-app.js` are references for earlier rendering and wiring, not replacements.
- A search found no `virus`, `virion`, `plate-preset`, or `erythrocyte` styles in `style.css`.
- `elementResultMarkup()` was not verified.

## Objective
- Extend GENESIS with rat, bird, tuna, influenza, and HIV presets while preserving its educational features.
- Clearly distinguish cellular presets from free virions and label simplified cellular mechanics as illustrative.

## Requirements
- Include all five presets with accurate explanations and visible source links.
- Preserve the DNA Codex, researcher progression, periodic table, and *Chlamydomonas*-inspired schematic.
- Bird and tuna presets represent nucleated erythrocytes; rat represents a hepatocyte.
- Influenza and HIV depict free virions—not host cells or infection progression. Viruses have no nucleus or organelles and do not divide independently.
- Virus presets must not advance through cell simulation or expose cell-only actions.

## Decisions
- Cell presets use illustrative cellular mechanics; virus presets show no cellular metrics or organelles.
- `loadPlatePreset()` distinguishes free virions from illustrative cellular presets in its toast.
- Virus plate entries are static particle schematics; no infection or division is modeled.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added five preset definitions, `makePresetPlate()`, `loadPlatePreset()`, and `activePlatePreset()` in `app.js`.
- Added `entityKind: 'cell'` to cells created by `makePlateState()`.
- Added DNA Codex navigation and researcher progression markup in `index.html`.
- Updated `plateCellMarkup()` and `cellView()` with virus-aware content, preset controls, explanations, citations, and separate virus/cell details.
- `node --check app.js` completed without syntax errors.

### Active
- Restore or implement missing rendering, navigation, event-handler wiring, and app initialization in `app.js`; current file ends at `genomeView()`.
- Guard simulation and all cell-only actions for virus presets; `tick()` still calls `advancePlateCells()` unconditionally.
- Verify or add virion, erythrocyte, and preset-control styles in `style.css`.
- Test preset selection, citations, persistence, navigation, and non-cellular behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore or implement app views and wiring in `app.js`, integrating existing presets.
2. Prevent virus presets from advancing/dividing or invoking cell-only actions.
3. Verify styles and test all presets, citations, navigation, and persistence.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Presets, rendering, simulation, and missing app wiring.
- `index.html`: Navigation, DNA Codex, researcher progression, and app mount point.
- `style.css`: Plate and cell visualization styles; preset and virion styling remains unverified.
- `/tmp/opencode/old-app.js`: Saved earlier `HEAD:app.js` reference for rendering, handlers, and initialization.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`, `genesis-latest.jpeg`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- Current `app.js` is only 97 lines; `git show HEAD:app.js` and `/tmp/opencode/old-app.js` are references for earlier rendering and wiring, not replacements.
- A search found no `virus`, `virion`, `plate-preset`, or `erythrocyte` styles in `style.css`.
- `elementResultMarkup()` was not verified.
